original.target_description: Study 6: facial competence and attractiveness predicting perceived prize-worthiness/work quality in a mixed-effects regression; numerical focal coefficients/p not available in obtained text.

n.sample_role: participants rating science articles; recruited N=824, exact analytic n after recognized-trial exclusions not established
n.quote: Study 6 ( N = 824 ) used the four physics news stories from study 3 with the least-extreme quality preratings, and the face stimuli from study 4.

replication.target_description: participants; within-participant competence effect on interest; authors’ post-replication report focal test.

n.sample_role: participants; within-participant competence effect on interest
n.exclusions: 15 excluded for technical issues; report labels statistic a t-test, but protocol deviations say replication result based on z-test due to software optimization differences.
n.location: Post-replication report p.2, Unplanned protocol deviations
n.quote: Unplanned Protocol Deviations: We have a sample size of 2213 participants, which is above our aim of 2085 participants. We excluded 15 participants who had technical issues (e.g., page loading problems). While we followed the pre-registered analysis exactly, the replication result is based on a z-test due to differences in the optimization routines implemented in different software applications (the replication result has been estimated in Stata, the original result in R). Other information: Since the experiment was expected to take less than 5 minutes, we had a show-up fee of $1.

es.quote: The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = 0.145 (95% CI [0.103, 0.187]).

p.quote: The hypothesis was tested using a t-test of the coefficient of the compe- tence variable in the mixed-effects regression (t(2209) = 6.822, p < 0.001).

reported_success.quote: Discussion: Given the criteria and procedure outlined above, the hypothesis of interest has been replicated at a significance level of p < 0.05.

notes: Original and replication evaluated separately. Replication statistics are as printed in the primary authors’ post-replication report. Replication targets original Study 4 (interest), whereas assigned original locator specifies Study 6 (work quality). Study 6 numerical effect and p not printed in obtained text; generic recruited N not treated as analytic n. Replication report labels the statistic t(2209), but its protocol-deviations paragraph describes a z-test; retained printed statistic with discrepancy.
